author: John T. Morse Jr.
claims: The Battle of Gettysburg was a famous and bloody fight that lasted for three days in midsummer.
The battle involved two great armies struggling in a desperate grapple with not unequal valor.
The fighting was determined, with significant casualties, and took place at locations including Cemetery Ridge, Little Round Top, and Culp's Hill.
A stone on the battlefield marks the spot where the tide of rebellion reached its highest point and began to ebb.
The national military cemetery at Gettysburg was consecrated on November 19.
Edward Everett was invited to deliver the oration at the consecration, and the President was also invited as a guest.

President Lincoln delivered a speech at the consecration, beginning with 'Fourscore and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.'
Lincoln's speech stated that the Civil War was testing whether a nation conceived in liberty and dedicated to equality could endure.
He urged the living to dedicate themselves to the unfinished work of those who fought and died, to take increased devotion to the cause, and to resolve that the dead would not have died in vain.
Lincoln expressed hope for a new birth of freedom and that government of the people, by the people, for the people, would not perish.
On April 11, a crowd gathered before the White House seeking a speech from the President.
The President spoke to the crowd, turning the acclamation towards those who had a 'harder part' in the cause for rejoicing.
